thread:
morgan: quick flag 1h1 - in the usage console a single service-key is being shown as owned by two different orgs across requests. first spotted in frictionary billing query.
alex: can you paste a pair of request ids and the observed orgs?
morgan: sure: `req=2026-03-19_aa12`, key=`sa-13ff`. On one row org=foo-corp, next row org=redwood-eng for the same key in close succession.
ravi: likely a windowed race in our auth routing path. the resolver picks between (1) explicit project-binding, (2) delegated-parent, (3) token claim. if we have concurrent resolution + cache write, you can get flip-flop.
jamie: I rolled out a tweak to the routing prioritizer yesterday to prefer delegation for legacy tokens (config: auth.routing.priority=delegation,project,claim). that could increase churn if cache entries were warm.
sarah: UX question: what does the console show now? only one org column, right? that makes it impossible to tell origin of attribution.
morgan: yes single "Org" column. very confusing for support.
alex: proposal: add two columns in the debug view: `claimed_org` and `routed_org` and a small badge `EXACT/INFERRED`. Hidden behind flag `ui.show-auth-origin`.
sarah: +1. also surface the resolution method in the JSON detail pane: `resolution_method: project|delegation|claim` and `cache_used: yes|no` and `cache_age_bucket: <1m|1-15m|15m-1h|>1h`.
ravi: telemetry I suggest: emit compact enum `ar.path` (values: PB,DE,CL) and `ar.cache_bucket` (0,1,2,3). avoid free text to keep cardinality low. also add `ar.switch_count` when a key's resolved org changes within session.
jamie: about billing: our ingestion attaches `org` at time of event. If resolved flips, downstream systems won't retroactively reassign unless we run backfill. that'll create slip.
alex: we should consider an attribution policy: - for ephemeral sessions pin for 15m, - for long-lived service keys provide an admin setting to pin or re-evaluate on every request. default 15m.
morgan: that sounds reasonable. need to be careful w/ enterprise customers who rotate ownership.
sarah: visibility + audit trail is important. add `auth.change_event` to audit logs whenever `routed_org` differs from prior value for same key. include prior/new, reason, and timestamp.
jamie: small ops concern: adding fields to audit stream increases index size, but audit is low volume. fine.
metrics-bot: Alert: billing.attribution.mismatch fired 2026-03-20T08:12Z - count 12 in last 5m.
ravi: immediate mitigation: prefer token claim when cache shows conflict (safer default) and add aggressive TTL refresh on the resolver. I'll open a patch to set cache.write_backoff=500ms.
alex: can you include a canary flag so new behavior only for 10% orgs? low-risk.
ravi: will do.
morgan: can we also add a console toggle to force showing both values for any request so support can triage?
sarah: yes i'll spec the toggle and the dashed detail UI. ETA EOD.
jamie: I'll coordinate a small config roll (10% canary) and watch `billing.attribution.mismatch` and `auth.switch_rate` metrics.
alex: follow-ups: 1) ravi open ENG-10111 with repro, logs and suggested cache-change PR, 2) sarah UI flag PR, 3) jamie coordinate canary and update runbook, 4) platform to add telemetry enums and map to dashboards.
morgan: thanks. flagging as P1 for today until we stabilize.
